page: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V, featuring 8 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16 instructions), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, while offering no bundled local storage and zero GPUs.

Benchmark testing highlights top-quartile single-core CPU execution, achieving a stress-ng single-core score of 3080.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2104.0, as well as strong small-model LLM generation speeds reaching 308.41 tokens per second. Multi-threaded throughput remains consistent within the median range, shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10979.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 20098.46. While cached memory read bandwidth is typical at 1186.58 GB/sec, uncached large-block reads register in the lower 25th percentile at 38.03 GB/sec, indicating latency constraints on non-cacheable data streams.

Due to the absence of integrated local NVMe disks, storage-bound workloads rely entirely on external network-attached volumes, introducing potential network overhead for disk-heavy processing. Cost efficiency is driven by the dedicated single-thread execution per core combined with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. This profile suits memory-intensive enterprise tasks, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, single-thread performance-critical compute tasks, and microservice compilation without necessitating large vCPU counts.
description: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v6 is a virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive and compute workloads, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding 8.0 GB per core. It integrates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with BF16 and VNNI support, alongside cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU hardware. Performance metrics demonstrate top-tier single-core compute capabilities in Geekbench and stress-ng, coupled with steady multi-core execution and high-throughput Redis operations. However, uncached memory bandwidth for large blocks drops to the bottom 25th percentile. The system is well adapted for in-memory databases, compiler toolchains, lightweight LLM token generation, and enterprise microservices requiring substantial memory capacity alongside single-threaded CPU efficiency.
